exposure: potentially traumatic childbirth experience (witnessed by non-birthing parent)
outcome: parent-infant relationship (levels of warmth and invasion)
cohort: The study included 312 non-birthing parents who were present for the birth of their first infant, with infants aged between 6 weeks and 12 months old.
finding: Non-birthing parents who experienced birth as potentially traumatic reported significantly higher CB-PTSD symptoms and felt a greater sense of invasion in relation to their infant, with CB-PTSD symptoms mediating the relationship between possible birth trauma and invasion.
cross-section timing: When the infant was between 6 weeks and 12 months old
